units.function: Pure tests for configurable attachment MIME allowlists, wildcard matching, content-type normalization, Office-type inference from filenames and the set of content types eligible for inline browser rendering.
units.dependencyDirection: Operator configuration and upload metadata enter normalization/matching helpers; routes use their result to admit uploads and choose inline versus download behavior, independent of storage or domain services.
units.keyDataModels: MIME type/pattern, wildcard, default allowlist, original filename/extension, octet-stream fallback, inferred Office MIME type and inline-safe content-type set.
units.lifecycle: Missing allowlist configuration falls back to images plus common Office types. Matching is case-insensitive and supports type or suffix wildcards and a global *. Generic binary uploads may be relabeled as Office documents from filename extension when the inferred type is allowed. PNG/SVG/PDF/plain text/MP4 are classified inline; HTML and ZIP are not.
units.testAssessment: Twenty-one concise cases cover parsing, normalization, wildcard behavior, legacy/current Office extensions, generic binary inference and inline classification. Missing are MIME parameters, malformed patterns, Unicode/double extensions, magic-byte or archive inspection, macro-enabled Office types, polyglots, decompression bombs, executable content, SVG/PDF active-content behavior, browser nosniff/CSP/sandbox/Content-Disposition and the danger of the global allow-all wildcard.
units.designRationale: Accept useful office and media attachments across inconsistent clients while retaining configurable admission and preventing obviously active or binary types from inline rendering.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS evidence and enterprise-data uploads are untrusted inputs whose admission, rendering, model ingestion and export must be governed separately and preserve the original bytes and declared/detected representations.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT normalization and table-driven parsing only. Do not treat client MIME or filename inference as trust; record declared, detected and normalized types, hash original bytes, quarantine and scan asynchronously, validate archives, enforce per-purpose policy and serve active formats from an isolated origin with nosniff, sandbox and attachment disposition. Disallow unrestricted * in managed production profiles.
units.responsibilityConflict: A filename can cause generic bytes to be relabeled as an Office document and several active-capable formats are called inline-safe without proving delivery controls. That weakens evidence integrity and can expose accountable reviewers when opening Agent-supplied artifacts.

units.function: HTTP upload tests for general Company assets and Company logos, including storage metadata, attachment limits, image-type rejection and SVG sanitization before persistence.
units.dependencyDirection: Multipart board requests enter asset routes; route validation/sanitization writes bytes through StorageService, persists metadata through AssetService and returns an opaque content endpoint path, with activity logging mocked at the boundary.
units.keyDataModels: Company id, namespace, original filename, content type, byte body/size, SHA-256, storage provider/object key, Asset creator/time metadata, content path and sanitized SVG DOM.
units.lifecycle: A board actor uploads multipart bytes into a Company namespace. General assets admit configured non-image attachments; logos require supported images, use the general size ceiling and sanitize SVG scripts, event handlers and external links before storage. Invalid type, oversize or unsanitizable SVG fails before Asset metadata creation.
units.testAssessment: Eight real-HTTP cases cover PNG/general text uploads, storage call shape, logo size boundaries, type denial and a useful malicious-SVG regression. Services/storage/authz are mocked. Missing are unauthenticated/cross-Company actors, multipart field/namespace traversal, actual MIME sniffing and hash verification, SVG namespace/CSS/data URL/entity/filter edge cases, malware/archive scanning, storage failure and orphan cleanup, database failure after object write, duplicate hash/idempotency, download authorization/range/cache headers, deletion/retention and audit emission.
units.designRationale: Provide one storage-backed asset abstraction for UI images and Issue attachments while making the highest-risk inline logo format safer and avoiding raw object-store identifiers in client-facing URLs.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs evidence/asset custody with tenant isolation, provenance, lifecycle and safe reviewer rendering; uploads may originate from humans, Agents, Connectors or enterprise data sources and carry different trust and retention rules.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT opaque asset ids/content paths, content hash metadata, pre-storage SVG sanitization and size tests. REIMPLEMENT ingestion as a staged Asset/Evidence pipeline: tenant-scoped authorization, temporary quarantine, byte sniff/hash/scan, transactional metadata plus recoverable object finalization, immutable provenance, retention/legal hold, purpose/data-contract link and isolated download/render service.
units.responsibilityConflict: The tests prove byte filtering but not who had authority to attach the artifact, whether the stored hash matches original or sanitized representation, or which Work/evidence contract owns it. Storage precedes mocked metadata creation without demonstrated compensation, so a failure can also leave untracked data.
